mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last 3 months signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last 3 months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over the last 3 months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as related sectors benefit.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over the last 3 months signals a weakening supply side, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic output slows.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real GDP (GDPC1) by more than 1% over the last quarter signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the quarters where GDP increases by more than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3% within the last month, it signals a robust labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in the last month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as real returns are eroded.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When retail and food services sales (RSAFS) increase by more than 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% within the last month, it signals strong consumer demand coupled with inflation, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer-oriented sectors benefit.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases > 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met.
